title: Introduce seqburst consolidator and occupancy timeline visualizer
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: We observed recurring short-duration concurrency spikes during seq-heavy workloads that were not captured cleanly by the existing flamepoint exporter. This PR introduces a lightweight 'seqburst consolidator' runner plus an occupancy timeline visualizer so we can (1) compress and annotate bursty sequences into coherent events, (2) attribute kernel occupancy and memory pressure across the burst lifetime, and (3) export compact timelines compatible with the lab's timeline UI.

What this implements: - A new runner: bench/seqburst/consolidator that takes raw session traces and consolidates adjacent short sequences into 'bursts' using a configurable time-gap and token-threshold heuristic. The output is a compact JSON event stream with per-burst metadata (primer-length, peak-concurrency, slot-occupancy, kv-checkpointed). - Occupancy timeline visualizer: tools/visualizers/occupancy_timeline.py renders burst events into an interactive HTML + SVG timeline suitable for manual inspection and inclusion in run artifacts. It highlights per-kernel occupancy bands and overlays memory pressure markers. - Flamegraph annotator: exporters/flame_annotator adds burst tags to existing per-kernel flame outputs so flamegraphs can be correlated back to bursts. - Integration glue: a new ingest path from consolidator -> aggregator that reduces artifact size by ~6x for highly bursty traces.

Design notes and tradeoffs: - The consolidator is intentionally lossy: it collapses micro-events to reduce downstream storage and highlight clinically relevant bursts. We preserve sample pointers so raw traces can be rehydrated when necessary. - Heuristics are tunable via config/seqburst.yaml (gap_ms, min_tokens, max_burst_duration_ms). Default values chosen after exploratory runs on production-like traces. - Visualizer is dependency-light (only uses d3 v7 and a tiny css bundle) to keep artifacts self-contained.

Testing and validation performed: - Unit tests covering burst detection edge cases (wraparound, nested bursts, extreme primer lengths). - E2E benchmark on a node with mixed sequence lengths (profile corpus: long-tail-2025). Compared baseline exporter vs consolidator path on the same traces: artifacts size reduced 5.8x and mean inspection time dropped by 72%. - Perf regression guard rails: added an automated smoke run in CI that runs the consolidator on a small sample trace and asserts output invariants (non-overlapping bursts, valid timestamps).

Checklist: - [x] Bench runner implemented and unit-tested. - [x] Visualizer + HTML artifact generation. - [x] Exporter annotated flames. - [x] CI smoke test and sample fixture added. - [x] Documentation: README with how-to, config knobs, and recommended workflows.

How to run locally: 1) python -m bench.seqburst.consolidator --input sample_traces/long-tail-2025.ndjson --output /tmp/bursts.ndjson 2) python tools/visualizers/occupancy_timeline.py /tmp/bursts.ndjson --out /tmp/occupancy_timeline.html 3) Open the HTML in a browser for interactive inspection.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the consolidator heuristics (bench/seqburst/consolidator.py) and the invariants asserted in tests/test_seqburst.py. The visualizer is intentionally minimal; UX improvements can be a follow-up (ENG-6899).

review_comments: Evan Park: Nice approach; two questions: can we preserve a sampled raw-event pointer for each burst so debugging is reversible? Also please add an invariant check that burst end >= start.
Luca Moreno: The HTML uses inline d3; can we avoid a CDN for reproducibility? Also suggest a thin color palette that's grayscale-friendly for prints.
Priya Rao: CI smoke failed once in my fork due to flaky fixture load (ndjson ordering). Can we add a sort step in the fixture loader?

perf_results_summary: E2E artifact comparison on long-tail-2025 (n=50 large traces): baseline exporter average artifact size 18.2MB -> consolidator path 3.14MB (5.8x reduction). Median manual inspection time per trace dropped from 2m18s to 39s. CPU overhead of consolidator on ingestion was 6.2% on average (acceptable for daily offline runs).

release_notes: Adds a new seqburst consolidator runner and occupancy timeline visualizer to the benchmark lab. Improves artifact compactness for bursty workloads and enables correlated flamegraph annotations. See docs/bench/seqburst.md for usage and config.
notes: Follow-up items: - Add interactive zoom/pan controls to the visualizer (ENG-6899). - Consider adding reversible rehydration path for on-demand full-trace expansion (ENG-6821).
